articles.title: SpaceX Prepares for Starship's 10th test flight: Texas launch expected at 6:30 p.m. CDT
articles.lede: SpaceX Prepares for Starship's 10th test flight: Texas launch expected at 6:30 p.m. CDT. SpaceX is preparing for the tenth flight test of its Starship spacecraft, with a launch window set to open as early as Sunday at 6:30 p.m. CDT from its Starbase facility in Texas.The launch, which follows investigations into the loss of a Starship during a previous flight and a static fire anomaly, includes hardware and operational changes aimed at increasing reliability.During the test, the Super Heavy booster will attempt a series of flight experiments on a trajectory toward a landing point in the Gulf. Unlike previous missions, it will not return to the launch site for a catch. The booster's primary test objectives will focus on its landing burn, including a test of backup engine functionality

articles.lede: SpaceX postpones Starship test flight over system issue. Elon Musk's SpaceX has called off the launch of Starship's tenth mission over an issue at its launch site, delaying an attempt to achieve several long-sought development milestones missed due to past tests ending in early failures. The 70m-tall Super Heavy booster and its 52m-tall Starship upper half sat stacked on a launch mount at SpaceX's Starbase rocket facilities in Texas as it was being filled with propellant ahead of a lift-off time. But roughly 30 minutes from lift-off, SpaceX said on X it was "standing down from today's tenth flight of Starship to allow time to troubleshoot an issue with ground systems." WATCH LIVE: SpaceX attempts to launch Starship rocket for 10th time
articles.lede: SpaceX has launched its latest test of the mega rocket Starship. It is the first-ever deployment of a test payload into space. Starship blasted off from SpaceX's launch site in South Texas on Tuesday night. The mission involved eight dummy satellites and was the 10th test for the world's biggest and most powerful rocket. It also included the successful return of the craft's booster, which splashed down in the Atlantic. The Starship itself remained in space with an expected splashdown soon in the Indian Ocean. SpaceX hopes to use Starship for future moon and Mars missions.

articles.title: 'It was disappointing:' Crowd reacts after SpaceX scrubs 10th Starship launch – again
articles.lede: SpaceX's planned Monday launch of its Starship rocket from Boca Chica, which would have been its 10th test flight, was canceled due to unfavorable weather conditions, disappointing dozens of spectators at Isla Blanca Park. This was the second consecutive scrub, following a Sunday cancellation due to a ground systems issue. While disappointed, spectators remain hopeful for the next attempt. SpaceX has announced a new target launch date for Tuesday, August 26, with a one-hour window beginning at 6:30 p.m. central time.
